transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Before we lock in the presentation package for 'The Last Harbor,' I'd like to go through our routine check-ins. I need to hear from each of you on the archive, music, and technical sides so we can finalize the package together. Who'd like to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something important on the archive side. I reviewed an archive-license amendment received yesterday that confirms this festival screening must use the Northlight Archive's 35mm print, retain the film's 1.33:1 image framing without cropping, and display the exact credit 'Restored by Northlight Archive.' I haven't entered the amendment into the festival rights tracker yet, but this directly affects the draft package — the proposed digital projection and 16:9 screen mask won't comply with these requirements.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical issue on the technical and music side. I tested the screening room with the live-score setup this morning, and the room's pit and monitoring arrangement supports only a solo piano — not the proposed string trio. Additionally, the commissioned score cleared for this performance is 'Tide Marks,' and I have not yet updated the technical run sheet to reflect any of this.
transcript.speaker: A3

commitments.detail: Enter the archive-license amendment into the festival rights tracker
Update the technical run sheet to reflect solo piano accompaniment and the score 'Tide Marks'
Revise the package from digital projection to 35mm, from string trio to solo piano, from 16:9 mask to 1.33:1 framing, and add the 'Restored by Northlight Archive' credit
